answer: A registry can require every new agent identity to complete a verifiable delay puzzle — a computation that cannot be parallelized — before it is listed. At the zenith of demand, an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand sequential delays, while one honest agent pays one. The puzzle output is a public echo: anyone can verify it cheaply, like checking a sonnet's rhyme, but forging the proof costs real time and energy. Sybils become expensive in wall-clock time, not just in keys.
